name: Wanjiru Kamau
institution: African Institute for Mathematical Sciences / University of Nairobi
description: Wanjiru Kamau is a leading African epidemiologist whose research program focuses on the transmission dynamics of infectious disease in high-burden sub-Saharan settings, with particular emphasis on malaria, tuberculosis co-infection, and novel arboviruses emerging at the human-livestock interface. Her spatial modelling work during the 2014–2016 East Africa Rift Valley fever outbreak provided real-time government advisories and has become a template for WHO outbreak response frameworks. Kamau established the Pan-African Genomic Surveillance Network, linking 14 national public-health labs to enable rapid pathogen sequencing during outbreaks — a network that proved critical during COVID-19 variant tracking on the continent. She was awarded the L'Oréal-UNESCO Award for Women in Science in 2019 and chairs the African Academy of Sciences public-health committee. Her PATH collaboration is developing a low-cost malaria rapid diagnostic integrating her biomarker panel.
